children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 17 years old, his eligibility depends on whether he's currently in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me what Alex is currently doing? For example, is he:
- Still in full-time education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent)?
- In an apprenticeship?
- In some other form of training?
- Working?
- None of the above?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in school anymore - he left after his GCSEs and hasn't gone on to do A-levels or anything like that. He's not working either, just at home at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 17 and has left education, there's one more thing that could affect eligibility. Has Alex registered with either:

- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or the Northern Ireland Careers Service), or
- The armed services?

If a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with one of these services, Child Benefit can potentially continue for up to 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have a couple more questions to confirm your circumstances:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question: Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, or any similar benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Age requirement**: Child Benefit normally covers children under 16. For those aged 16-19, it can continue only if the child stays in **approved education or training**.
- **Alex's situation**: Since Alex is 17 and has left education without continuing into A-levels, college, or other approved education or training, he no longer meets the criteria.
- **Careers service option**: There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex hasn't registered with either of these.

**What you could do next:**

If Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he registers. Alternatively, if Alex decides to return to approved education or training, you could become eligible again at that point.

I hope this helps clarify things. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old, which means he is over the standard age limit of 16 for Child Benefit. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can normally continue only if the child stays in approved education or training. Alex has left education after his GCSEs and is not in any approved education or training. Additionally, Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, which would have allowed Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after leaving education. Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and is not receiving benefits in his own right, but these factors alone do not restore eligibility - the child must be in approved education/training or registered with a careers service/armed forces to qualify at age 17. Since none of these conditions are met, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
